record.body:
## Interfaces

The new surface is tests/test_library_e2e.py. It shells out to adaptive-artifacts resolve, init, and create, then to orchestra close-batch with --cwd set to the temp repo. The only product edit is an evidence-binding record type on contract/project-design.json (orchestra/data/project-design.json is a symlink to it), which setup copies into the temp store so affidavit.binding.bind_observation can write project:evidence-binding. orchestra close-batch stays an in-process call from orchestra.cli to close_batch.main; the test never invokes that function itself.

## Assumptions

Graded only the scoped brief's phase, specification, design, decisions, work items, and acceptances against the diff and tree. Acceptance verify_commands were treated as intent, not as executed results. No execution-report, check-run, or assignment text was used. Human-witness claims are treated as a valid claim-gate pass under affidavit.verdict.run_verdict. Sibling trees ~/affidavit and ~/adaptive-artifacts were read as the libraries the phase assumes are already on main; the test was not run.

## Invariants

Command close and Python close both accept the same fixture — not established. The test runs only the command and asserts exit 0. Library inspection of orchestra.close_batch, affidavit.verdict.run_verdict, affidavit.binding.recheck, and adaptive_artifacts.project.open_store shows in-process imports; subprocess argv on that path is git or ssh-keygen, not aff or adaptive-artifacts. That shell-out ban is not locked by the new test.

## Conflicts

The specification says R1–R6 are one integration test that calls the Python close and fails if it starts aff or adaptive-artifacts. The work-item acceptances split R4 and R6 into external python -c checks, and the R6 checks ignore the Python close status. The tree follows that split.
